{"metadata":{"description":"Run DeepSeek Harness Web UI on your home LAN — 4 minimal patches + one-click apply/revert scripts | 让 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web UI 在局域网跑起来","id":"gh:1333573136","install_available":false,"language":"Shell","name":"deepseek-harness-lan","slug":"oitsukiii/deepseek-harness-lan","topics":["agent","bash","deepseek-harness","dsh-plugin","home-network"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Run DeepSeek Harness Web UI on your home LAN — 4 minimal patches + one-click apply/revert scripts | "},{"id":"p1s2","text":"让 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web UI 在局域网跑起来"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# 🐾 deepseek-harness-lan"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"**English** | 简体中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"> Run DeepSeek Harness Web UI on your home LAN — bind a specific IP, trust it, and open it from any "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"eepSeek Harness Web UI on your home LAN — bind a specific IP, trust it, and open it from any device."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"> **🎯 Target version: dsh `0.1.2-rc.1` (commit `a66e470204`)** — the patch is written and verified a"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"gainst this version; other versions may break (see 🧩 Compatibility)."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## 📖 What is this"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"dsh's Web UI is **officially restricted to localhost access only**. `--host 0.0.0.0` fails immediate"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"'s Web UI is **officially restricted to localhost access only**. `--host 0.0.0.0` fails immediately:"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"This is a **deliberate security design** — the dsh Web UI sits on top of an agent that can execute a"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"rbitrary commands, and the official project does not want it exposed to the network."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"But what if you want to open dsh from **Windows, phones, or tablets** on your home/office LAN? This "},{"id":"p10s2","text":"repository provides **3 minimal patches + one-click scripts** that let you bind a **specific LAN IP*"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"* and run the dsh Web UI safely."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## ✨ Features"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"- 🔧 **3 minimal diffs** — only the necessary source changes, no extra dependencies (two of the origi"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"nal four LAN changes were adopted upstream by 0.1.2-rc.1: `--trusted-host` CLI + `trustedHosts` fenc"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"e in `rpc-host.ts`, so those files are no longer patched)
- 📦 **One-click apply / revert** (`apply.s"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"h` / `revert.sh`) — auto-detection, duplicate-application guard
- 🧩 **Does not break the official se"},{"id":"p12s5","text":"curity model**: the `0.0.0.0` wildcard is still rejected; the `--trusted-host` explicit trust mechan"},{"id":"p12s6","text":"ism is preserved
- 🧪 **Verified on dsh 0.1.2-rc.1**: full `pnpm run build`, page load, API calls, an"},{"id":"p12s7","text":"d privileged endpoints all pass
- 🪄 **Auto-installs the missing build dependency** (`unrun`) so `pnp"},{"id":"p12s8","text":"m run build` doesn't fail mysteriously"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"### Why it works without patching"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"dsh's trust check (browser-trust) **looks at the request's Host header, not the source IP** (DNS reb"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"inding defense); and `crypto.randomUUID` is only available in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost)."},{"id":"p14s3","text":" An SSH tunnel makes the browser always access dsh via `127.0.0.1`, so:"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| Three gates | Under SSH tunnel | Why |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"| Gate 1 (CLI/schema) | ✅ not triggered | dsh listens on `127.0.0.1` = official default, no changes "},{"id":"p16s2","text":"ema) | ✅ not triggered | dsh listens on `127.0.0.1` = official default, no changes needed |
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## 🔒 Security notes (please read)"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"- ⚠️ **This UI can execute arbitrary commands**. After patching, **any device on the LAN** can acces"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"s and control your agent.
- ✅ Only use it on a **trusted home/office network**.
- ❌ **Do not** port-"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"forward 3080 to the public internet (port forwarding / DMZ).
- ❌ **Do not** use `--host 0.0.0.0` (st"},{"id":"p18s4","text":"ill rejected after patching — a deliberately kept line of defense).
- 💡 Advanced: put an **authentic"},{"id":"p18s5","text":"ating reverse proxy** (e.g. nginx Basic Auth) in front of dsh.
- 🔐 `--trusted-host` is the official "},{"id":"p18s6","text":"browser-trust mechanism's explicit trust entry — only fill in your own LAN IP."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"## 🧩 Compatibility"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"**This patch is written and verified against dsh `0.1.2-rc.1` (commit `a66e470204`).**"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"> ✅ **Upstream note (0.1.2-rc.1)**: two of the original four LAN changes were adopted upstream — the"},{"id":"p21s2","text":" CLI now has `--trusted-host` and `packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts` checks `this.trustedH"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"osts` instead of an empty list — so the current patch set is down to **3 files**:
>
> 1. `packages/h"},{"id":"p21s4","text":"ost/webserver/src/index.ts` — widen the bind-host schema from two literals (`127.0.0.1`/`0.0.0.0`) t"},{"id":"p21s5","text":"o `string` (LAN IPs);
> 2. `apps/web/src/main.ts` — `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill for plain-HTTP LAN "},{"id":"p21s6","text":"serving;
> 3. `packages/client/tsdown.client.ts` — `REPOSITORY_ROOT` via `process.cwd()` instead of "},{"id":"p21s7","text":"`import.meta.url` (fixes the workspace manifest lookup when tsdown compiles this preset with `unrun`"},{"id":"p21s8","text":" into `node_modules/.unrun`, which otherwise breaks the build with `no packages/*/*/package.json dec"},{"id":"p21s9","text":"/.unrun`, which otherwise breaks the build with `no packages/*/*/package.json declares the name …`)."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"> ⚠️ **Known upstream build quirk (0.1.2-rc.1)**: on a clean checkout, the full `pnpm run build` may"},{"id":"p22s2","text":" fail with `Cannot find entry: ["lib/types/{index,invariant,startup}.js"]` attributed to `@deepseek-"},{"id":"p22s3","text":"ai/dsh-root`. Cause: leftover directories from older dsh versions (e.g. `packages/client/runtime`, `"},{"id":"p22s4","text":"packages/host/apiproxy`) that were removed upstream but survive `git checkout` because they contain "},{"id":"p22s5","text":"only ignored files (`node_modules`). Fix: remove the stale directories (`git clean -ndx <dir>` to li"},{"id":"p22s6","text":"st, then delete), then rebuild."},{"id":"p23s1","text":"- Verification chain: patch applies cleanly (`git apply --check`) → full `pnpm run build` succeeds →"},{"id":"p23s2","text":" Web UI page load → `/api` calls → privileged endpoints (`settings.describe`, etc.) all pass.
- dsh "},{"id":"p23s3","text":"upstream iterates fast; **other versions will most likely break**:
- When the source context changes"},{"id":"p23s4","text":", `apply.sh`'s `git apply --check` **fails and aborts safely** without dirtying your repo (this is a"},{"id":"p23s5","text":" protection mechanism, not a bug).
- **Adapting to new versions**:
1. Run `apply.sh` on the new vers"},{"id":"p23s6","text":"ion and note the conflicting files when it fails;
2. Manually adapt by following the "three gates" a"},{"id":"p23s7","text":"pproach in 🧠 How it works;
3. PRs with adapted patches are welcome.
